q: What is this tool?
a: A free tool that looks at a text or an image and tells you whether it was probably made by artificial intelligence. It also shows you why, point by point.

q: Is it free?
a: Yes, completely free. No subscription, no paid tier, no advertising.

q: Do I need an account?
a: No. There is no account, no password, no sign-up. You open the page and use it.

q: Where does my text go when I paste it?
a: Nowhere. It stays on your device. We never receive it and never store it, because nothing is sent to us.

q: Does it work offline?
a: Yes, after the first visit. The small analysis program is saved on your device. Put your phone in airplane mode: the tool keeps working.

q: Why a number instead of a simple yes or no?
a: Because nobody can answer yes or no reliably. The tool gives you an estimate from 0 to 100 and shows the clues behind it.

q: What does "4 out of 100" mean?
a: That the text looks like human writing in 96% of cases. The number shown is the AI probability, not a grade of your text.

q: Why is a text I wrote marked as AI?
a: It happens. Very polished, academic or administrative writing looks like what machines produce: sentences of the same length, neutral phrasing. It is not a judgement about you.

q: Which languages are supported?
a: Seven interface languages today: French, English, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch. The structural analysis works in many more languages, but the lists of typical phrasings are mainly French and English.

q: How does it pick the language?
a: From your browser's language, then from the site you came from. You can always change it in the menu at the top.

q: Does it work on a phone?
a: Yes. On a small screen the layout adapts: the text on top, the analysis below.

q: Can I use it for homework?
a: You can use it to understand how a text comes across. But never hand in a detector result as proof: it is not reliable.

q: Can a teacher use it to grade?
a: They can use it to start a conversation, never to decide alone. A detector is wrong in both directions.

q: I'm accused of cheating, will the tool clear me?
a: No, and no tool will. This site helps you understand the clues, not win an argument. Talk to the person involved.

q: Can it really tell the difference?
a: It spots writing habits: even rhythm, repeated phrasings, calibrated paragraphs. That is strong evidence of a style, not proof of authorship.

q: Why does AI always write the same way?
a: It keeps picking the most likely wording. The result is smooth, even text with the same tics over and over.

q: What if I rewrite the text by hand?
a: The score usually drops, because rewriting adds irregularity. That is expected: the tool measures style, not who wrote it.

q: What is the sentence highlighting for?
a: Sentences are coloured by how suspicious they are. Hover one and a small bubble explains what drew attention.

q: Why are some sentences red?
a: Because they stack up clues: a typical phrasing, an average length, a list of three items, a connective at the start.

q: What is "burstiness"?
a: Mixing short and long sentences. People do it naturally. Machines produce an even rhythm. The English word stuck because there is no good equivalent.

q: What is the "model fingerprint"?
a: An estimate of which family of model may have written the text: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic or Meta. It is a tendency, not an accusation, and it is often wrong.

q: Why does the fingerprint say "indeterminate"?
a: Because the text is too short or too neutral to separate the families. The tool would rather assert nothing.

q: What about the image side?
a: It first looks for an official AI signature inside the file. If that information was erased, it analyses the pixels, which is far less reliable.

q: Why is my image "unsure" and not "AI"?
a: Because without an official signature nothing can be proven. We would rather say so than accuse wrongly.

q: What is C2PA?
a: A signature some cameras and generators write into the file. It survives sharing as long as nobody strips it.

q: Why do so many images have no signature?
a: Because social networks, screenshots and format conversions erase that information. Its absence proves nothing.

q: What is the artefact map?
a: A view that exaggerates the image's invisible detail. Areas that are unnaturally smooth or noisy can give away a generated image.

q: Do you store anything about me?
a: No identifier, no profile, no history of your texts. There is no tracking cookie and no advertising.

q: Who can see what I analyse?
a: Nobody but you. The analysis runs in your browser, in front of you.

q: Can I use it at work?
a: Yes. The code is permissively licensed and you can also run it on your own servers.

q: How do you make money?
a: We don't. No ads, no resold data, no paid tier. It is an open project.

q: Is this legit or a scam?
a: There is nothing to install, nothing to pay, nothing to enter. The code is public: anyone can check that it does what it claims.

q: Can I copy the code?
a: Yes, the MIT licence allows it: reuse, modify, even sell, as long as you keep the licence notice.

q: What is this invisible-character thing?
a: Some tools hide invisible characters in a text to fool detectors. We find them and show you the exact code points.

q: What is a homoglyph?
a: A letter that looks like another. A Cyrillic "a" instead of a Latin "a", for example. Identical to the eye, different to a machine. Often a sign of tampering.

q: Why is the word count sometimes surprising?
a: Chinese, Japanese and Korean do not separate words with spaces. We then count each character as a word, the way word processors do.

q: Can I analyse a very long text?
a: Yes. The main analysis is near-instant. The second, heavier analysis only processes an excerpt to stay fast.

q: Why is the second analysis slow the first time?
a: Because it downloads about 460 MB, once. The language-model juror is optional: the rest of the jury works without it. After that everything is instant and works offline.

q: Can I turn the second analysis off?
a: Yes. Just don't run it: the tool works entirely without it and nothing is downloaded.

q: What are "layer 1" and "layer 2"?
a: Layer 1 is the instant calculation, always available. Layer 2 is a second, heavier program that gives an extra opinion. The jargon is ours, not yours.

q: Does the tool send my text to the model maker?
a: No. The program is downloaded once, then it works on your machine. Your text never leaves.

q: Does it work for homework in Chinese or Arabic?
a: Partly. Sentence rhythm, paragraph length and invisible characters are measured in every language. The lists of typical phrasings are not.

q: Why does the interface change language on its own?
a: It follows your device language. If you prefer another, pick it in the menu: your choice is remembered.

q: Why are some languages missing from the menu?
a: Because a language only appears once its translation is complete. We would rather a language be absent than half-translated.

q: Can I contribute a translation?
a: Yes, it is the most useful way to help. Each language fits in a single file, and an automatic check says whether it is complete.

q: I'm a developer, how do I integrate it?
a: The engine is a TypeScript module with no heavy dependency, with one entry point per tool: text analysis, image analysis, word count.

q: Where is the code?
a: On GitHub, link at the bottom of the page. Everything is public, including the change history.

q: Can I host it myself?
a: Yes. It is a static site: a handful of files, no application server needed.

q: How do I report a bug?
a: On GitHub by opening an issue, or on Discord. A concrete example helps enormously.

q: Can the tool be wrong?
a: Yes, in both directions. It can miss edited AI text and flag very formal human writing. That is why the score is never presented as proof.

q: Why not just give a "reliable" percentage?
a: Because that would be a lie. A single number with no margin gives false confidence. We would rather show the clues and their weight.

q: Could a scammer use this?
a: They can try to lower a score, but that is a bad bet: edited text is still edited text. And nobody can forge a valid C2PA signature.

q: What if a site accuses me without evidence?
a: Ask for the method, not the score. A verdict with no explanation is worth nothing, here and everywhere else.

q: Is the text I paste saved anywhere?
a: No. Close the tab and it is gone. We have no way to recover it, because we never had it.

q: Why ask me to check in airplane mode?
a: Because you don't have to take our word for it. Cut your connection and see for yourself that everything keeps working.
